title: Reconstruction of the computation snapshots
statement: Let $M$ be an oblivious finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with $k$ work tapes and a fixed binary code for its optional states. Let $m,T \in \mathbb{N}$, let $a : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be an assignment, and let $y$ be a Boolean word of length $m$. Suppose the raw block at time zero encodes the initial snapshot of $M$ on $y$; for every $t<T$, the state slice of the raw block at time $t+1$ encodes the next state determined by the block at time $t$; and, for every $t\le T$, the input slice gives the input symbol scanned in the run on $y$, while each work-tape slice gives the symbol prescribed by the most recent visit to that tape's current head position (or blank if there has been no such visit). Then for every $t\le T$, the raw block at time $t$ is exactly the encoding of the snapshot of the run of $M$ on $y$ at time $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is an oblivious finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
A fixed binary code for the optional states of $M$
$y$ is a Boolean word with length $m$
The raw block at time zero encodes the initial snapshot on $y$
For every $t<T$, the state slice at time $t+1$ encodes the next state from the block at time $t$
For every $t\le T$, the input slice agrees with the scanned input symbol in the run on $y$
For every $t\le T$ and each work tape, the work slice agrees with the symbol prescribed by the last visit to the current head position, or is blank if there is no such visit
replaced: Let the machine be oblivious, let $y$ have length $m$, and suppose an assignment's raw blocks satisfy: the block at time zero is the encoded initial snapshot; the state meaning at every $t < T$; the input-slice equations at every $t \le T$; and the work-slice equations at every $t \le T$ on all tapes. Then for every $t \le T$ the raw block at $t$ equals the encoding of the genuine snapshot of the run on $y$ at time $t$; junk blocks are excluded bit for bit.
